what: A pin can only be written safely after the store's first scan since it opened: before it `Store::pins()` is empty, so writing a pin of a name replaces the keys an earlier run pinned. Every writer of a pin has to know this (the daemon requeues the keys for the next build's end; the import has to flush and end periods until a scan ran, before its first put).
cost: about an hour reading collect.rs to find it; an import must force a scan first
cause: a pin is a whole record per name, newest wins, and the name's current keys are known only from a scan
whys: the import wrote a pin and could have dropped earlier keys
pins are found by scanning packs, not through an index by name
a pin's key is a hash of its contents, so the name's newest cannot be looked up
the pin form was designed for one writer that always runs after a scan
class: an API that is only correct after a hidden precondition (read-modify-write of a record whose current value may not be loaded)
prevention: `Store::pin_add(name, why, when, keys)` in blaze-cas that merges with the name's pin itself and refuses, or waits, until the pins are read; asked of lane storegc. Until then `serve::packs::stored::pins_read` holds the rule for imports.
workaround: pins_read: flush and end periods (bounded) before the first put
fix: lane storegc wrote `Store::pin_add` / `Store::pins_read` (crates/blaze-cas/src/collect.rs, not compiled); packs call it through `serve::packs::stored::pin_grown` and their own merge is deleted
state: fixed in the tree, unverified until the round builds
